candidates.title: Benchmarking Large Language Model Inference on Limited-Resource Edge Systems
candidates.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly considered for deployment on edge and limited-resource systems, where local inference can reduce latency, improve privacy, and decrease dependence on cloud infrastructure. While prior studies have evaluated either task accuracy or hardware efficiency in isolation, few benchmarks combine generation-based response-quality evaluation with real-device power measurements on a representative limited-resource platform. This study addresses that gap by benchmarking twelve compact and mid-scale open-weight LLMs (sub-1B to 8B parameters), evaluating generation-based accuracy on a desktop platform and measuring deployment efficiency—throughput, power consumption, and energy use—on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Super; the accuracy–efficiency trade-off is thus established at the model-configuration level. Unlike prior Jetson-based evaluations relying solely on internal telemetry, this work pairs generation-compatible lm-eval accuracy tasks with a dual power-measurement setup that combines internal tegrastats rail readings with external board-level input power measured using a digital multimeter and explicitly compares GPU-accelerated and CPU-only inference modes. GPU-accelerated inference provided a clear advantage, increasing median throughput from 7.12 to 18.13 tok/s and improving external-meter energy efficiency from 0.453 to 0.823 tok/J, despite higher mean input power. Sub-1B models offered the best throughput and energy efficiency, whereas 7–8B models achieved stronger accuracy at a substantially higher energy cost per generated token. These results demonstrate that edge LLM deployment requires multi-objective evaluation balancing accuracy, throughput, power consumption, and energy efficiency.
candidates.reason: 資源制約エッジでのLLM推論ベンチマークとしてJetson Orin Nano上で12モデルのスループット・消費電力・エネルギーを実測し精度と効率のトレードオフを示す、推論基盤の計測に当たる研究である

candidates.title: ParallelPrefill: Efficient LLM Prefill on Mobile NPU via 2D Task Decomposition on Hexagon DSP
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 International Conference on Machine Learning and Neural Networks
candidates.abstract: On-device large language model (LLM) inference on mobile devices is increasingly bottlenecked by the prefill phase, which processes the entire input prompt before generation begins. While existing systems offload decode-phase operators to the Qualcomm Hexagon DSP, prefill remains largely single-threaded due to an incomplete parallelization of the Flash Attention and matrix multiplication kernels. We identify two root causes: (1) Flash Attention parallelizes only along the KV-head dimension, leaving the query-length dimension—which dominates during prefill—unexploited; and (2) the output transfer from VTCM to DDR after matrix multiplication is serialized on a single DSP thread, creating a write-back bottleneck that grows linearly with matrix size. We present ParallelPrefill, a system that addresses both bottlenecks through two contributions. First, we redesign the Flash Attention task decomposition from 1D (KV heads only) to 2D (query positions × KV heads), enabling all available DSP hardware threads to participate in prefill computation. Second, we parallelize the VTCM-to-DDR output transfer in the matrix multiplication kernel using a work-stealing scheduler over row-tile chunks. Together, these changes reduce prefill latency by up to 2.7 × on Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Qwen2.5-1.5B with a 512-token prompt, while decode performance is unaffected. On Qwen2.5-3B with a 512-token prompt, ParallelPrefill achieves 3.1 × and 2.7 × higher prefill throughput than llama.cpp and MNN-LLM, respectively, on the same device.
candidates.reason: ParallelPrefillはモバイルNPUのHexagon DSP上でFlash Attentionをクエリ位置とKVヘッドの2次元に分解し行列積の書き戻しも並列化することで、オンデバイスLLMのプリフィルを最大2.7倍高速化するシステムである

candidates.title: SP³: Enhancing Structured Pruning via PCA Projection
candidates.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
candidates.abstract: Structured pruning is a widely used technique for reducing the size of pre-trained language models (PLMs), but current methods often overlook the potential of compressing the hidden dimension (d) in PLMs, a dimension critical to model size and efficiency. This paper introduces a novel structured pruning approach, Structured Pruning with PCA Projection (SP3), targeting the effective reduction of d by projecting features into a space defined by principal components before masking. Extensive experiments on benchmarks (GLUE and SQuAD) show that SP3 can reduce d by 70%, compress 94% of the BERTbase model, maintain over 96% accuracy, and outperform other methods that compress d by 6% in accuracy at the same compression ratio. SP3 has also proven effective with other models, including OPT and Llama. Our data and code are available at an anonymous repo.
candidates.reason: SP3は主成分射影による構造化プルーニングで隠れ次元を圧縮し、BERTを94%圧縮しつつOPTやLlamaでも有効とされ、モデルサイズと推論時の計算・メモリ削減に直結する推論向け圧縮手法である
